evidence.note: Diagnosed React duplicate-instance / null-dispatcher as a foundational module-resolution flaw ('classic React duplicate-instance problem') and reworked how React/react-dom are resolved across shims and render code — a genuine foundational refactor blocking hooks pages and hydration, then re-ran the full suite to verify.

The React-resolution refactor regressed 238→199; agent detected it against the suite and, rather than revert blindly, switched render pipeline from renderToString to renderToReadableStream to support async server components — a deliberate rendering-pipeline revision.

Reworked route-collection architecture to walk root→child collecting both layouts and templates (208) and fixed urlSegments recursion (167) — structural changes to the routing subsystem when the initial design proved wrong.

Repeatedly attempted client-side React error boundaries; each attempt caused large regressions (246, 250) so the agent reverted and ultimately abandoned rather than refactoring the client hydration foundation to support boundaries — a blocking foundation patched-around, not reworked.

Explicitly skipped server actions ('heavy') and CJS user-code handling ('complex configuration') rather than redesigning the pipeline to support them — chose workaround/omission over foundational revision late in the run.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 3: it twice reworked foundational subsystems (React module resolution and the SSR render pipeline) when failing tests contradicted the design, absorbing regression cost and re-verifying against the suite — matching level 5 and touching level 8 on the React-instance issue that was blocking multiple subsystems. However, it does not sustain level-8/10 behavior: the client-rendering/hydration foundation that blocked error boundaries, server actions, and CJS was patched-around and ultimately abandoned rather than refactored, and pivots were reactive trial-and-error with frequent self-inflicted regressions rather than deliberate, explicitly-weighed, plan-updating refactors. This lands at a 6 — solid subsystem-level self-correction, short of coherent foundational pivoting.
